Definition: from a presumed derivative of G3806; something undergone, i.e. hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence:-- affection, affliction, motion, suffering.
BiblicalUsage: Pathema is suffering, something undergone, hardship or pain. Paul says in Romans 8:18 that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. In 2 Corinthians 1:5 the sufferings of Christ abound in us, and so does our consolation. Peter says in 1 Peter 1:11 that the Spirit testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ and the glory that should follow, and in 1 Peter 5:1 he calls himself a witness of the sufferings of Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sufferings of Christ and the sufferings of His people are joined in this word: His first, and ours after Him, and the glory that follows is greater than both. That is why I hold that present suffering is not the last word, it is the weighed word, and the glory outweighs it.
